questions.prompt: What kind of energy is stored inside a battery?
questions.explanation: Inside the cell, chemicals hold energy; the reaction turns it into electrical push when the circuit closes.
questions.misconception: Batteries feel 'electric' but their stored form is chemical, converted at work time.

questions.prompt: The two ends of a battery are called its...
questions.explanation: A battery has two terminals, + and −; their energy-level difference is the voltage.
questions.misconception: Compass directions and generic names are wrong; + and − are the only true labels.

questions.prompt: A 9 V battery is made of 1.5 V cells. How many are inside?
questions.misconception: The pack's total volts can trick you into '9 cells'; it is 6 × 1.5 V.

questions.prompt: While the battery powers the bulb, its chemical layers...
options: Shrink as the energy is used
questions.explanation: The reaction spends the chemicals, so the layers shrink and the push fades over time.
questions.misconception: Batteries don't lose a substance: they lose spent reactants, which is what 'drained' means.

questions.prompt: Which pair of numbers describes a battery?
questions.explanation: Volts (push) and capacity in mAh (stamina) are the two ratings that matter.
questions.misconception: Physical size is not the rating; a small cell can push the same volts as a big one.
